name: Malachi

overview.author: Malachi, whose name means “my messenger” (1:1).
overview.date: About 460–430 BC, likely around the time of Nehemiah, after the second temple was rebuilt.
overview.audience: The postexilic community in Judah, including careless priests and spiritually indifferent people.
overview.setting: The temple stood, but worship had become cold and routine. Priests offered blemished sacrifices, men divorced their wives, people withheld tithes, and many questioned God’s justice.
overview.purpose: To affirm God’s covenant love, confront hollow worship and covenant unfaithfulness, and announce the coming messenger and the day of the LORD.
overview.structure: Six disputations in which God makes a statement, the people question it (“But you say...”), and God responds, followed by a closing exhortation.

themes.title: God’s Covenant Love
themes.text: “I have loved you,” says the LORD (1:2).

themes.title: Honoring God in Worship
themes.text: God rejects blemished offerings and halfhearted service.

themes.title: Faithful Leadership
themes.text: Priests should guard knowledge and teach truth.

themes.title: Faithfulness in Marriage
themes.text: “I hate divorce,” says the LORD (2:16), as faithlessness.

themes.title: Generosity
themes.text: Withholding tithes is robbing God; God invites them to test Him.

themes.title: God Does Not Change
themes.text: “For I the LORD do not change” (3:6).

themes.title: The Coming Messenger and Day
themes.text: God will send His messenger and Elijah before the great day.

christInBook.text: The messenger who prepares the way is John the Baptist, and the Lord who comes to His temple is Jesus (Mark 1:2; Matthew 11:10).
Elijah’s coming is fulfilled in John the Baptist (Matthew 11:14; Luke 1:17).
The sun of righteousness rising with healing points to Christ (Luke 1:78–79).
God’s name great among the nations is fulfilled through the gospel of Christ.

crossReferences.note: John the Baptist prepares the way.
John in the spirit of Elijah.

reflection: When you hear “I have loved you” from God, what is your honest response?
Are you giving God your best or your leftovers (1:8)?
How does Malachi 2:14–16 shape your view of faithfulness in marriage and promises?
What would it look like to “test” God in generosity (3:10)?
How do you speak with others who fear the Lord (3:16)?

chapterList.title: I Have Loved You
chapterList.summary: God says, “I have loved you,” but the people ask, “How have you loved us?” God points to His choosing of Jacob over Esau. Then He rebukes priests who despise His name by offering blind, lame, and sick animals. “Offer that to your governor.” God’s name will be great among the nations.
questions: Why do the people doubt God’s love (1:2)?
What do blemished offerings reveal about the heart (1:8, 13)?

chapterList.title: Unfaithful Priests and Spouses
chapterList.summary: God rebukes priests for not honoring Him; a true priest’s lips guard knowledge. The people are faithless to one another, marrying foreign idol-worshipers and divorcing the wife of their youth. “For the man who does not love his wife but divorces her... covers his garment with violence.” They weary God by saying evildoers are good.
questions: What should mark a godly leader (2:5–7)?
Why does God care so much about marriage faithfulness (2:14–16)?
How do we weary God with our words (2:17)?

chapterList.title: The Messenger and the Book of Remembrance
chapterList.summary: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me.” The Lord will come suddenly like a refiner’s fire. “For I the LORD do not change.” God calls them to return and bring the full tithe: “Put me to the test.” Those who feared the LORD spoke together, and a book of remembrance was written before Him.
questions: How is 3:1 fulfilled in John the Baptist and Jesus?
Why does God say they are robbing Him (3:8–10)?
What does God promise those who fear Him (3:16–18)?

chapterList.title: The Sun of Righteousness
chapterList.summary: The day is coming, burning like an oven for the arrogant. “But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings.” Remember the law of Moses. God will send Elijah before the great and awesome day, to turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers.
questions: What is the day of the LORD like for the arrogant and for those who fear God?
How is Elijah’s coming fulfilled (Matthew 11:14; Luke 1:17)?
Why might the Old Testament end with turning hearts of fathers and children?

tagline: “I have loved you,” says the LORD: a call to wholehearted worship
readingPlan: 4 chapters: one chapter a day takes 4 days; two a day takes about 2 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
